name: Al Qal'a of Beni Hammad
description: High in the Hodna Mountains of northern Algeria, about 225 km southeast of Algiers, lie the ruins of a hilltop city that was the Hammadid dynasty's first capital. Founded in 1007 and destroyed in 1152, it was ringed by roughly 7 km of walls. Visitors can still see its vast mosque, a 20-metre minaret and the remains of the emir's palace with its gardens and pavilions.
